summary: Hold, and set depends_on to cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-grouped-s2-finite-fix. It re-implements the same unfixed correctness work and also widens the gate into shapes where the kernel has never run a single correct tile. Widening is worth a check only after finite-fix reaches M1 at >=128 and shows the N=16/32 buckets correct and competitive.
justification: The motivation is real: Marlin at bs=8/16/32 is 114.0/176.1/207.5 us against floors of 37.3/52.5/70.8, and decode_32 is master's weakest load. The mechanism claimed is weak, though. 'The persistent grid streams each touched expert's weight once, which Marlin's m-block scheme lacks' is not true at small M: with 1-8 routes per local expert, Marlin's single m-block per expert also streams each touched weight once. Marlin's gap at small M is more plausibly occupancy and latency (few experts x N-tiles over 132 SMs, short K loops). This kernel's 1-producer/2-consumer, 4-stage, BK-128 pipeline with a 64-row M per warpgroup does not obviously fix that: at bs=8 under EP8 roughly 6-8 experts x (I/64) w13 items is a few hundred items over 132 CTAs, with pipeline fill costs on each. The direct evidence is negative: the persistent swap-AB mma.sync sibling, with the same weights-on-M idea and the same 132-CTA grid, ran correctly at T<=32 and was 1.7-2x SLOWER than Marlin (LESSONS 2026-10-25, REWRITE_READ 01:04Z), and the prefill wgmma grouped GEMM was 1.8x slower than Triton. WEAKEST LINK: the bs 8-32 'faster' expectations rest on an untested premise, and the kernel has never produced a correct tile in any bucket. Bundling the gate change with the finite fix means a correctness failure in the small-M buckets (N=16/32, never exercised: the canary used only N=128) is confounded with the large-M fix. Separate flags reduce that but do not remove it, and the 8 extra self-check sizes add prepare time and log volume to a log that is only a 15 KB tail.
confounders: triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack / align-parallel-per-expert-verify: at 8 <= T <= 32, master uses the fused _align_small Triton align. The wgmma path replaces it with expert_map gather + moe_align_block_size + gather (3 launches), which at small M is a measurable fraction (several us out of 114-207). The replaced-kernel sum must include it, and it biases against the rewrite.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: at T < 32 master uses the Triton _post_norm_combine_kernel, but _moe_wgmma always calls SGLang's fused norm. Widening the gate to 8-31 silently reverts that landed gain on bs=8/16 unless the wgmma path keeps master's small-M norm branch. This is a definite regression source that would be misread as the GEMM losing.
marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: no effect below 128 (SGLang's block pick is kept there).
interference: No ab companion now. The right sequencing is a dependency, not a companion: run finite-fix first. With the merged design from the finite-fix review, its self-check covers buckets 16/32/64 at M=256 skewed and prints prepare-time per-kernel timing. Mint the widened gate only if that run shows (i) N=16/32-bucket items correct and (ii) wgmma per-kernel prepare time at a small-M-like routing that beats Marlin. A cheap way to get (ii) without widening the gate is to time the wgmma kernels in finite-fix's prepare at synthetic M=8/16/32 routings as well (print only, no enable). That turns this hypothesis's premise into data at zero extra check cost. When re-minted, keep master's small-M post-norm and align branches on the wgmma path for T < 32.
rules_flags: None in itself. Its own bound constant is required (LESSONS 2026-10-25): do not derive the 8 from ALIGN_FUSED_MAX_TOKENS or SMALL_M_POST_NORM.
open_questions: Why is Marlin far from the floor at bs=8-32: occupancy/latency, or bytes? If occupancy, a split-K or more-CTAs-per-expert scheme is needed, which this kernel does not have.
Does the bs=33 test and the verify_1 bs=8 shape weight justify the extra self-check time and the larger rules surface before M1 exists at >=128?
